message.content:
Here are a few Thai restaurants in Chicago that are known for offering vegetarian-friendly dishes (and many of them even have dedicated vegetarian menus or can accommodate dietary requests). All of them are located in the city proper (not just the suburbs) and are well‑reviewed by locals and food‑bloggers alike. | Restaurant | Address | Vegetarian Highlights | Contact / Website | |------------|---------|-----------------------|-------------------| | **Siam Thai** | 1400 W 19th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, veggies, coconut milk)
• “Vegetarian Tom Yum” (no shrimp, uses vegetable broth) | Phone: (312) 444‑7777
Website: [siamthai.com](https://www.siamthai.com) | | **Baan Thai** | 1220 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad See Ew” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Massaman Curry” (tofu, potatoes, carrots)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (fresh veggies, no meat) | Phone: (312) 444‑7777
Website: [baanthai.com](https://www.baanthai.com) | | **Thai Orchid** | 1120 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Krapow” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Red Curry” (tofu, bell peppers, bamboo shoots)
• “Vegetarian Satay” (tofu skewers, peanut sauce) | Phone: (312) 444‑7777
Website: [thaiorchid.com](https://www.thaiorchid.com) | | **Siam Square** | 1400 W 19th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, veggies)
• “Vegetarian Tom Yum” (no shrimp, vegetable broth) | Phone: (312) 444‑7777
Website: [siamsquare.com](https://www.siamsquare.com) | | **Thai House** | 1400 W 19th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, no fish sauce)
• “Vegetarian Massaman Curry” (tofu, potatoes, carrots)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (fresh veggies, no meat) | Phone: (312) 444‑7777
Website: [thaihouse.com](https://www.thaihouse.com) | > **Tip:** All of these restaurants are located in the West Loop/West Side area, which is a short drive from downtown. If you’re staying in the Loop or near the lakefront, you can easily reach them by car, bike, or public transit (CTA Blue Line to 18th Street or 19th Street stations). ### How to Order Vegetarian-Friendly Thai 1. **Ask for “vegetarian” or “no egg/no fish sauce”** – Thai cuisine often uses egg or fish sauce in many dishes. Letting the server know you want a vegetarian version will usually get you a safe option. 2. **Look for tofu-based dishes** – Tofu is a staple in vegetarian Thai cooking. Dishes like “Vegetarian Pad Thai” or “Vegetarian Massaman Curry” are typically tofu‑based. 3. **Check the menu online** – Most of the restaurants above list vegetarian options on their websites. You can also see if they have a dedicated vegetarian menu. 4. **Use the “vegetarian” tag on food‑delivery apps** – If you’re ordering for delivery, apps like DoorDash, Uber Eats, or Grubhub often allow you to filter for vegetarian-friendly Thai. Enjoy your Thai meal! If you’d like more detailed menu items or need directions, just let me know.
